screening_protocol.aoi: 25 km × 25 km city-center screening box; approximate WGS84 bounding box, ~625 km²
screening_protocol.screening_gate: At least 90 distinct acquisition dates for metadata discovery. Passing this gate does not establish valid pixels, flood events, independent reference labels, or inclusion in final analyses.
screening_protocol.balanced_design: For enrolled event studies: same 25 km × 25 km (~625 km²) analysis footprint and prespecified event/baseline rules; require at least 3 QA-valid acquisition dates in each period, each with at least 80% unmasked pixels in the fixed AOI and each asset footprint. When more than 3 dates qualify, select the same number per area using a consistent temporal rule and report all exclusions/missingness. If any area cannot meet the minimum, defer it or reselect before analysis; do not impute. Independent labels must be collected from government/field records not derived from the same satellite product.

results.screening_rationale: Gulf coastal compound rainfall, river, and surge flooding; critical infrastructure exposure is well documented.
results.value_integration_question: Use as a high-hazard coastal baseline and test how observed-water overlap aligns with infrastructure and watershed planning.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: Houston’s FY2026–2030 CIP estimates $1.156 billion for storm-drainage improvements, with about $170 million for Local Drainage Program and Storm Water Action Team projects. The plan describes objective ranking of flood-protection needs and design for 2-year collection-system rainfall while reducing structural-flood risk during 100-year events.
results.value_dimensions: drainage service continuity; capital-project prioritization; neighborhood-level exposure
results.validation_path: Overlay only city-published drainage project and channel/detention geodata available for the 25 km study box; compare event-period satellite classifications with city/USGS gauge records and dated official flood reports. Record geometry/date coverage before analysis.
results.scope_limit: CIP allocations are planned estimates, not measured reductions in flood loss; the plan cautions that receiving-system capacity can still cause flooding.

results.screening_rationale: Coastal rainfall flooding interacts with groundwater table, high tides, and sea-level rise; NOAA-supported research targets prediction and risk management.
results.value_integration_question: Test a shallow-groundwater coastal setting and compare satellite water signals with documented local flood evidence.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: NOAA NCCOS reports a rainfall-flood model demonstrated over roughly 1,000 km² of Miami-Dade using rain, gauges, topography, land use, flood infrastructure, and groundwater. For a four-day May 2020 Memorial Day flood period, canal water levels were predicted with about 15 cm average accuracy and the model ran at least 30 times faster than real time.
results.value_dimensions: canal and drainage operations; groundwater-sensitive neighborhoods; equitable risk-management prioritization
results.validation_path: Use documented gauge/canal levels, rainfall timing, and independently mapped event reports for a held-out event; treat the NOAA 2020 experiment as contextual precedent, not as ATLAS ground truth or performance evidence.
results.scope_limit: The NOAA demonstration is county-scale and predates the current candidate window; it does not validate the 625 km² candidate box or ATLAS.

results.screening_rationale: USGS documented widespread Milton flooding in its Tampa coverage area, major-stage rivers, and field measurements/gage repairs.
results.value_integration_question: Test an event with independent hydrologic measurements and coastal/river flood context.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: USGS deployed eight wave sensors between Naples and Crystal River to measure Hurricane Milton coastal impacts and added a rapid deployment gauge in St. Petersburg; USGS also documented post-storm flood measurements and gauge repairs along Florida’s Gulf Coast.
results.value_dimensions: coastal water level; transport and utility access; recovery prioritization
results.validation_path: Match any candidate-box OPERA dates to USGS/NWS gauge time series and geolocated high-water marks or official event reports. Keep regional instruments outside the box as context and do not count them as local reference samples.
results.scope_limit: The cited sensors cover a regional coast and do not establish adequate independent labels inside the Tampa candidate box.

results.screening_rationale: Low elevation, levees, pumps, and a large catch-basin network create a documented urban rainfall-flood management problem.
results.value_integration_question: Test satellite screening in a pump-dependent, leveed urban drainage environment.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.need_evidence_type: municipal hazard plan and operating context
results.empirical_evidence: The City hazard-mitigation plan identifies six flood types and reports 24 city pump stations with total design capacity of 50,891 cfs. It also records 69 significant flooding events in 1997–2019 using NOAA Storm Events data, while warning that some NOAA damage fields are unreliable.
results.value_dimensions: pump-dependent drainage service; road and emergency access; low-lying community exposure
results.validation_path: Pre-register one dated event and baseline, then compare eligible OPERA pixels with city pump/drainage records, NWS rainfall and river stages, and dated official street-flood reports where spatial precision is sufficient.
results.scope_limit: The historical event count is not a geocoded independent truth set, and the City notes limitations in the NOAA records; pump design capacity is not actual operating capacity during any event.

results.screening_rationale: NOAA-hosted research maps present/future flood adaptation areas; infrastructure and power-system exposure are documented.
results.value_integration_question: Test dense coastal infrastructure and compare pluvial/coastal water exposure across an urban asset portfolio.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: NYC DEP’s December 2025 report identifies 86 priority drainage areas in its 2024 Stormwater Analysis and reports 325 FloodNet sensors plus 241 sewer monitors citywide. The monitoring supports flood tracking and sewer performance work; agency counts are not local to the candidate box.
results.value_dimensions: critical sewer and transport service; neighborhood drainage priorities; public sensor coverage
results.validation_path: Acquire dated FloodNet and NYC DEP records, independently review their spatial coverage against the 625 km² box, and validate a held-out event against municipal inundation or high-water labels rather than using capital-plan priority zones as truth.
results.scope_limit: The agency’s counts are citywide and do not imply that all sensors or priority areas fall within the candidate AOI.

results.screening_rationale: The Sacramento region relies on levees along major rivers; USGS maintains streamgages and studies flood processes in California’s Central Valley.
results.value_integration_question: Add an inland river/levee comparator and assess whether water observations can complement gauge-based context.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: California DWR describes more than 1,600 miles of State and federal levees in the Central Valley and more than 70 overtoppings or breaches since 1983; its flood-risk communication program sends notices to at-risk parcel owners across 17 counties.
results.value_dimensions: levee-protected communities; transport and utility corridor exposure; risk communication
results.validation_path: Use local Sacramento River/American River gauge and levee incident records, DWR floodplain layers, and event-date reference extents; exclude regional counts from the local denominator.
results.scope_limit: These metrics describe the broader Central Valley program, not the city-center AOI, and the cited page does not provide a local event-label dataset.

results.screening_rationale: The City’s 2025 comprehensive plan calls for stormwater management and flooding mitigation, including capital and watershed actions.
results.value_integration_question: Test an inland urban-runoff case and connect exposure evidence to watershed and public-infrastructure planning.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.need_evidence_type: municipal watershed planning and event response
results.empirical_evidence: Atlanta Watershed Management publishes ten watershed improvement plans that identify infrastructure needs and recommended projects. City emergency communications also document active monitoring of road, drainage, and public-safety conditions during heavy-rain flooding; this is direct management relevance but not a quantified citywide loss series.
results.value_dimensions: watershed and drainage investment; road access; neighborhood service equity
results.validation_path: Map plan project and stormwater geographies in the candidate box; evaluate a predeclared event using NWS rainfall, USGS stream gauges, and dated city incident/closure reports with location-level inclusion rules.
results.scope_limit: Plan coverage and agency response do not establish customer demand, parcel-level impacts, or independent event accuracy.

results.screening_rationale: NOAA/NWS river gauge documentation defines flood stages and describes levee/floodwall impacts along the Mississippi.
results.value_integration_question: Test a major-river and levee comparator with official river-stage context.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: NWS reports that the Mississippi River at St. Louis crested at 49.58 ft on August 1, 1993, then a record, during the region’s Great Flood. This provides a strong riverine/floodwall stress context for an inland comparator.
results.value_dimensions: river and floodwall exposure; regional transport continuity; long-term flood preparedness
results.validation_path: Use NOAA/NWS gauge records and recent dated event reports for actual validation; retain 1993 as contextual extreme-event history, not as a contemporaneous label for the 2024–2026 screen.
results.scope_limit: The headline evidence is historical and regional; it does not establish recent local flooding or current demand.

results.screening_rationale: Greater Jakarta faces regular widespread flooding alongside water-supply deficits and water-quality challenges; the World Bank calls for integrated urban water management.
results.value_integration_question: Study cross-jurisdictional water exposure and the integration of flood, water-supply, sanitation, and infrastructure planning.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.need_evidence_type: municipal flood-response capacity and multilateral research
results.empirical_evidence: DKI Jakarta reported 580 stationary pumps across 202 locations and 557 mobile pumps across its five administrative cities in 2024. The World Bank describes Greater Jakarta as a 14-municipality/district, three-province system facing recurring floods alongside water-supply and sanitation challenges, and calls for integrated urban-water management.
results.value_dimensions: pump and drainage operations; water quality and supply; cross-administration planning
results.validation_path: Obtain dated BPBD flood-event and pump-operation records, rainfall and river/gate levels, then spatially resolve them to the fixed AOI. Engage local technical partners to review translation, data licensing, and location bias.
results.scope_limit: Pump counts are response-capacity inventory, not utilization or measured effectiveness; Greater Jakarta evidence spans well beyond the selected box.

results.screening_rationale: PUB documents flash/coastal flood risks, investments in drainage, a national flood-resilience program, and extensive sensor monitoring.
results.value_integration_question: Test a data-rich, highly urbanized setting where satellite screening can be compared with agency sensors and flood reports.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.need_evidence_type: national drainage performance and current risk context
results.empirical_evidence: PUB reports that flood-prone area fell from about 3,200 ha in the 1970s to less than 25 ha, a 99% reduction. Its 2 April 2025 national list names 36 flood-prone locations defined as low-lying areas with a history of flooding. These are Singapore-wide management and residual-risk context, not event-specific label data or ATLAS results.
results.value_dimensions: drainage-service performance; urban transport and facility access; residual-risk hotspot prioritization
results.validation_path: For a held-out event, obtain dated PUB flood alerts, water-level sensor or rainfall records, and official geospatial hotspot layers. The 2025 PDF supplies named locations but no event-specific extent geometry; verify licensing and geocode only from a suitable official or openly licensed source before testing intersection with the frozen common box.
results.scope_limit: The national 1970s-to-current area trend and 36 named locations cannot be attributed to the 625 km² screen without geospatial intersection. The hotspot list is risk context, not an independent event label or pixel-level reference.

results.screening_rationale: Dubai Municipality’s AED 30bn Tasreef program expands stormwater collection and drainage; contracts cover critical urban areas.
results.value_integration_question: Test rapid urban growth and major drainage investment, while treating dry-climate extreme rainfall as an event-based case.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: Dubai Municipality reports AED 1.439 billion in contracts across four Tasreef phases, more than 36 km of planned new drainage lines with contracts expected complete by 2027, and an estimated AED 30 billion total program cost. Its 700% discharge-capacity increase is a long-term design target over the next 100 years, not an observed performance result.
results.value_dimensions: stormwater tunnel and network service; critical technology/logistics facilities; capital phasing and residual risk
results.validation_path: Acquire municipality project alignments, construction status, rainfall, and dated incident/road-closure records; stratify completed and under-construction assets before any exposure analysis.
results.scope_limit: Published capacity values are future program targets and cannot serve as observed flood truth or current system performance.

results.screening_rationale: India approved an urban flood risk mitigation program that includes Mumbai; city planning and IFLOWS document substantial flood research and warning needs.
results.value_integration_question: Test monsoon, coastal, drainage, and asset exposure; join satellite screening to the city’s flood-warning and mitigation evidence.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: India’s August 2026 UFRMP Phase I announcement includes Mumbai, with a city allocation of ₹707.71 crore and ₹150 crore reported released at that point. It documents funded implementation need; project completion and measured outcomes remain pending.
results.value_dimensions: drainage and flood-risk reduction; transport and public-service continuity; implementation equity across neighborhoods
results.validation_path: Use BMC/Maharashtra dated rainfall, drainage works, pump/gauge operations, and geocoded flood incident records; separately identify pre- and post-project dates and verify data translation and spatial resolution.
results.scope_limit: Approval and release establish program activity, not completed works, reduced flooding, or customer demand.

results.screening_rationale: World Bank city-region analysis documents interacting upstream runoff, intense local rainfall, and tidal effects.
results.value_integration_question: Test a deltaic megacity where river, pluvial, and tidal drivers overlap and require cross-system interpretation.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: World Bank urban-flood analysis describes Bangkok risk as the interaction of large upstream runoff, intense local rainfall, and tidal influence, with major flood-control works built following past floods. This makes the city a useful compound-driver comparator.
results.value_dimensions: urban drainage and river operations; commuter and utility access; upstream-to-city coordination
results.validation_path: Acquire Royal Irrigation Department and Bangkok Metropolitan Administration gauge, rainfall, pump, and event-closure records. Predefine local ground-truth sources and normalize Thai local time/date before matching satellite acquisitions.
results.scope_limit: The source is a planning/assessment report with historical context, not a current independent event label or an evaluation of ATLAS.

results.screening_rationale: World Bank work documents Tokyo-region urban flood risk management practice and the need to integrate risk into urban planning and investment.
results.value_integration_question: Test a mature infrastructure context and evaluate water-screening evidence alongside risk-informed planning and engineered controls.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: Tokyo Metropolitan Government reports that by October 2025 it had 30 operational storage basins across 14 rivers with about 2.73 million m³ capacity, plus about 12 km of diversion channels. It targets about 3.65 million m³ of total capacity by fiscal 2035 to address floods from rainfall above 50 mm/hour.
results.value_dimensions: storage and river-control infrastructure; dense transport and utility service; investment tracking
results.validation_path: Use Tokyo river/flood telemetry and rainfall with event reports and storage-facility service areas; assess source timestamps, datum and Japanese date/time conventions before event matching.
results.scope_limit: Capacity is metropolitan inventory/target, not proof of local flood absence or a satellite-classification accuracy measure.

results.screening_rationale: World Bank-supported Metro Manila Flood Management Project targets 17 cities/municipalities and more than one million people with pump/drainage upgrades.
results.value_integration_question: Test a high-need urban drainage and pumping portfolio with documented public investment and operations context.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.empirical_evidence: The World Bank describes the Metro Manila Flood Management Project as covering 17 cities/municipalities and targeting more than one million people through pumping-station, drainage, solid-waste and control-system improvements.
results.value_dimensions: pump-station service; drainage and solid-waste interactions; population and neighborhood access
results.validation_path: Obtain project pump and drainage locations, PAGASA rainfall, city/BWSC incident reports, and independently reviewed event extents. Resolve Metro Manila boundaries against the fixed city-center box and report only in-AOI evidence.
results.scope_limit: Project beneficiaries and footprint are regional targets, not actual affected persons or performance inside the candidate box.

results.screening_rationale: World Bank case material documents urban flood exposure, drainage constraints, and the need to combine structural and nonstructural measures.
results.value_integration_question: Test an inland megacity and connect observed-water evidence with drainage, land-use, and asset planning.
results.status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
results.need_evidence_type: municipal drainage plan and investment pipeline
results.empirical_evidence: São Paulo’s October 2026 drainage-plan release describes 201 interventions, 173 priority works, and a projected R$16.51 billion program through 2049. A separate municipal update reports 389 interventions completed since 2021; plan and commitment totals describe public management activity, not measured flood-loss reduction.
results.value_dimensions: stormwater works and maintenance; transport and community service; project priority and equity
results.validation_path: Join dated municipal flood incident and rainfall records to geocoded interventions; separate completed/active/planned works, and validate a held-out event against independently reviewed high-water or flood-extent data.
results.scope_limit: Municipal project totals are citywide, may span the candidate box unevenly, and are not measured reduction in risk or proof of ATLAS demand.
